title: Cheitharol Kumbaba (Royal Chronicle of Manipur) Tangkhul Records
title_translation: Historical Chronicle Entries on Tangkhul-Meitei Relations
creator: Royal Scribes of the Palace of Kangla
publisher: Kangla Palace Archives / Manipur State Archives
notes: Centuries-long official court chronicle recording diplomatic ties, coronation ceremonial exchanges of Haora cloths, trade routes, and customary treaties between valley kings and Tangkhul chiefs.

english_translation_text: The Cheitharol Kumbaba (Royal Chronicle of Manipur) records centuries of official state interactions with Tangkhul chiefs.
It meticulously documents royal coronation gift exchanges, presentations of woven Haora cloths, joint defensive campaigns, and border pacts.
The chronicle provides invaluable written archival verification of the oral fraternal traditions linking hill and valley peoples.
chronicle_milestones: 1. 15th Century: Early reign entries recording Tangkhul chieftains attending royal durbars at Kangla Palace.
2. 16th–17th Century: Customary treaty protocols established; exchange of spearheads, brass gongs, and Haora robes.
3. 1734: King Garibniwaz formalizes hill-valley trading posts along the foothill passes.
4. 1891: Anglo-Manipur War records noting Tangkhul political stances and border realignments.
5. Archival Preservation: Maintained in archaic Meitei Mayek manuscripts in Manipur State Archives.
historical_significance: The primary indigenous court archive validating centuries of continuous political, economic, and ceremonial relations.

historical_terms.Haora: Traditional red-black-white ceremonial cloth presented to royalty
historical_terms.Khamasit: Peace treaties and mutual non-aggression covenants
historical_terms.Ning-khamathan: Reciprocal state gifts honoring sovereign leaders
